text:
Maya (Support): Hey team, customer ACME-app reported a bunch of 5xx responses from the hosted inference API starting ~10:20 UTC. They see gateway 502s and some 504s. They say it started after a normal traffic spike. We have request id examples: req=aa12, bb34. Can someone triage?

Jude (SRE): looking. Are these user-facing 5xx from router or from the model backend? Any traces?

Maya (Support): The app gave back: "502 Bad Gateway - upstream returned error" and sometimes "504 Gateway Time-out". Customer supplied this curl: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` -> 502.

OpsBot: Incident alert created: INC-2026-0425-17 (auto). Severity: P2. Affected customers: ACME-app (trial).

Kai (Eng-runtime): I pulled a few request IDs from logs. See intermittent 502s coming from control-plane auth/session lookup failing with a downstream 5xx from the session-store/proxy. Sample log: ```
2026-04-25T10:21:03Z router.INFO req=aa12 route=/v1/generate status=502 upstream_error=auth-proxy(502)
Caused-by: auth-session-cache: conn=timeout, code=504
```

Priya (Eng-infra): ConfigDB also shows elevated p99 latency around that time. I'm seeing a flurry of SELECTs from routing-policy service hitting the config DB with open connections spiking. Possible connection pool exhaustion.

Jude (SRE): That matches. We have two control-plane deps in sequence for each request: auth/session lookup -> routing policy resolve -> config DB for dynamic routing. If the auth cache becomes slow it cascades. Any recent deploys to auth-proxy or routing-policy?

Kai (Eng-runtime): No deploys on runtime in the window. There was a rolling update to routing-policy service 3h before, but it passed canaries. Could be a cache eviction storm on the auth layer (redis TTL miscalc) after the traffic spike.

Maya (Support): Customer is asking for ETA and workaround. They are hitting 502s roughly 20% of requests for a few minutes.

Jude (SRE): Quick mitigation steps I recommend: 1) Enable auth-proxy read-through cache fallback (flip feature flag) to allow stale session reads for 30s. 2) Temporarily increase upstream timeout gateway->auth from 1s to 2.5s. 3) Scale out session-cache replicas (add 2x) if autoscale available. 4) Add retry-on-502 for 1 retry with jitter client-side for idempotent calls.

Priya (Eng-infra): I can scale config DB read replicas and bump the connection pool size for routing-policy service. Doing now (scaling +2 replicas). I'll also check for any long-running queries.

Kai (Eng-runtime): I'll prepare a targeted rollback of the routing-policy rolling update and hold new canaries, and also enable the auth-proxy fallback. Pushing a flag now.

Maya (Support): I've informed ACME-app: suggested they retry transient 5xxs and enabled a short circuit for fallback model routing (we can route to regional fallback) — they accepted.

Jude (SRE): Running quick diagnostic queries: ```
# conn pool usage
SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE application_name='routing-policy';
# slow queries last 5m
SELECT pid, now()-query_start AS dur, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE now()-query_start > interval '2s';
```
Found a few long-ish read transactions from a batch job around 10:16 that overlapped the spike. Killing the one long batch helped free connections.

OpsBot: Action: routing-policy rollback in progress (task id rp-rollback-209).

Kai (Eng-runtime): auth-proxy fallback flag is enabled. Starting to see auth-proxy 502 counts drop. Metrics: auth-proxy error-rate 5xx -> 1.2% (was 18%).

Priya (Eng-infra): DB replicas are up. Connection pool usage back to normal. p95 query latency down from 1.8s -> 210ms.

Maya (Support): Customer confirms traffic mostly healthy now, error rate down to ~0.5%. They want postmortem and permanent fix.

Jude (SRE): Next steps for postmortem: - timeline of events - root cause hypothesis: concurrency spike + long-running batch job + routing-policy pool sizing + auth cache TTL eviction mismatch -> cascade - list mitigations (pool sizing, better backpressure, circuit breaker on routing-policy, read-through cache fallback by default for short duration, retry strategy guidance to customers) - SLA impact & notify.

Kai (Eng-runtime): I'll open ENG-RUNTIME ticket to: a) add circuit breaker around routing-policy calls, b) add metrics/alerts for auth cache miss storms, c) make read-through fallback opt-in default during high latency windows.

Priya (Eng-infra): I'll open ENG-INFRA ticket to increase default routing-policy DB pool and add connection timeout throttling for batch jobs. Also recommend we add maintenance window for heavy batch queries.

Maya (Support): I'll draft customer-facing RCA and share once eng tickets are created. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

OpsBot: Incident INC-2026-0425-17 transitioned to RESOLVED by Jude (SRE). Resolution summary: auth-session-cache flapped under spike causing routing-policy queries to cascade to config DB; mitigations included auth-proxy fallback, DB replica scale, routing-policy rollback.

Jude (SRE): Leaving an evidence snippet for the postmortem: ```
10:16 batch-job started -> connection pool saturation (routing-policy)
10:20 auth cache TTL eviction -> increased miss rate -> extra reads to config DB
10:21 router 502s spike -> fell after fallback + db scale + rollback
```

Maya (Support): Great, I'll follow up on customer comms and link the eng tickets. Closing thread after PM review.

Kai (Eng-runtime): Thanks everyone, will include recommended config values and safety checks in the postmortem.

Priya (Eng-infra): added remediation checklist to infra ticket.

Maya (Support): Thread closed.
